(i) hepatic lipase is required for the clearance of remnants from the circulation and (ii) in the absence of hepatic lipases, the accumulation of remnants in the plasma of animals on a high-fat, high-cholesterole diet is the result, in part, of saturation of hepatic lipolytic activity by abnormally high amounts of chylomicron-derived remnants.

the accumulation of cholesterol-rich remnants in the plasma of hypercholesterolemia rabbits is due to saturation of the available enzyme, hepatic lipase; and that the accumulation of these remnants can be reversed by exogenously added hepatic lipase.

hepatic lipases are essential for the rapid removal from circulation of remnants of triacylglycerols-rich lipoprotein particles, and that the accumulation of cholesterol-rich remnants in the plasma of hypercholesterolemic rabbits is the result of a saturation of the available enzyme.

the role of hepatic lipoprotein lipases in the metabolism of lipoprotein remnants.
the metabolism and function of the lipoproteins that transport cholesterol and other lipids in the plasma.
the elucidation of the mechanisms by which the liver takes up lipoprotein remnants.

hepatic lipases are essential for the normal removal of chylomicron and very-low-density lipoprotein remnants, and that hepatic lipoprotein lipases are also essential for the normal clearance of beta-VLDCs.
hepatic lipases are essential for the normal clearance of remnants from circulation.

the accumulation of plasma cholesterol in the hypercholesterolemia of rabbits is a consequence of a failure in the clearance of chylomicron-derived cholesterol-rich beta-remnants by the liver, which is due to saturation of hepatic lipolytic enzymes by the large amount of triacylglycerols present in the circulation.

hepatic lipoprotein lipoprotein lipolytic activities are required in concert for the efficient clearance of remnants from the circulation.
